question: A downhill test bench launches a sled whose mass plate reads 45000 g. The control number is the smaller root of x^2 - 14x + 48 = 0, and multiplying that root by 6 gives the sled's speed in metres per second. The energy the moving sled carries is the base value, which the display shows in kilojoules. From that displayed figure 19 is subtracted for the brake allowance and then 22 for the track allowance, both in those same kilojoule units. The bench room holds a 35 L compressor tank that plays no part. What does the display finally show, in kJ?

A paper mill report ends with one number in newtons. A reel of mass 142 kg is accelerated on the winder. Its acceleration, in metres per second squared, is found by writing out 2k - 1 for k running from 1 to 8 and adding the eight values together. The drive must supply the force that gives that reel that acceleration. Eight reels run per winder, 6 winders run per mill, and the group has 8 identical mills. What number ends the report, in N?

A test bench sets its trolley speed from a control number: the smaller root of x^2 - 10x + 16 = 0. From that number the technician subtracts 19, then adds 9, and then adds 20. The value that comes out is the trolley's speed in metres per second. The trolley has a mass of 26 kg. The bench also carries a 14 L coolant bottle that plays no part. What energy, in J, does the moving trolley carry?

A hydro plant report ends with one number in kilojoules. A gate whose mass plate reads 15000 g moves at a speed, in metres per second, equal to the exact area under the curve y = 2x^2 + 2x between x = 0 and x = 3. The energy the moving gate carries is the base value, which the report writes in kilojoules. Eight gates work the intake, so the intake figure is 8 times that record. From the intake total 1 is subtracted for the seal allowance and then 19 for the machine allowance, both in those same kilojoule units. What number ends the report, in kJ?

A quarry hoist accelerates a bucket of mass 80 kg at a rate, in metres per second squared, equal to the larger root of x^2 - 9x + 8 = 0. The rope must supply the force that gives that bucket that acceleration, and the log records that force in kilonewtons. Nine hoists work a face, and the site has 4 faces. The site's water bowser holds 550 L, which is not involved in this. What is the site total, in kN?

A rowing tank tests a shell whose mass plate reads 60000 g. Its speed, in metres per second, is 2 multiplied by the sum of 8 and 3. The energy the moving shell carries is the base value, to which 9 J stored in the rigger is added. Five shells are tested per session, so the session energy is 5 times that corrected value, and the club holds 10 identical sessions. What is the club total, in J?

A textile mill report ends with one number in kilonewtons. A beam whose mass plate reads 17000 g is accelerated on the loom. Its acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the exact area under the curve y = 3x^2 + 8x between x = 0 and x = 1. The drive must supply the force that gives that beam that acceleration. Five beams run per loom, so the loom force is 5 times one beam's figure, and the report writes that in kilonewtons. A shed holds 12 looms, and the mill has 12 sheds. A 300 L sizing vat serves the shed and plays no part. What number ends the report, in kN?

A glassworks sheet ends with one number in kilonewtons. Two batches of 314 and 24 identical panes are packed into equal full crates, using the largest crate size that divides both counts exactly. A carriage of mass 192 kg is then accelerated at a rate, in metres per second squared, numerically equal to that crate size. The drive must supply the force that gives that carriage that acceleration; 22 N of clamp preload is added to it, and 17 N of rail drag is subtracted. The sheet writes the result in kilonewtons and then adds 19 in those same kilonewton units for the standing tare. The annealing lehr runs at 540 degrees Celsius, which is not used. What number ends the sheet, in kN?

A cold-store rig accelerates a pallet of mass 107 kg at a rate, in metres per second squared, equal to the smaller root of x^2 - 10x + 16 = 0. The drive must supply the force that gives that pallet that acceleration. Nine pallets run per aisle, so the aisle force is 9 times one pallet's figure, from which 7 N is subtracted for the roller drag. The store has 10 aisles, and 17 N is then subtracted from the store total for the dock tare. The store is held at 4 degrees Celsius, which is not used here. What is the final figure, in N?

A tanker depot report ends with one number in kilonewtons. Two lots of 397 and 268 identical drums are grouped into equal full stacks, using the largest stack size that divides both counts exactly. A carriage whose mass plate reads 197000 g is then accelerated at a rate, in metres per second squared, numerically equal to that stack size. The drive must supply the force that gives that carriage that acceleration, and 12 N of it is lost in the rollers and subtracted. The report writes the remainder in kilonewtons. Six carriages run per bay, and the depot has 3 bays. What number ends the report, in kN?

A brewery audit ends with one number in kilojoules. A cask of mass 40 kg rolls along the stillage at a speed, in metres per second, equal to the smaller root of x^2 - 9x + 8 = 0. The energy the moving cask carries is the base value, which the audit writes in kilojoules. Four casks share a rack, 6 racks make a cellar, and the brewery has 6 cellars. The auditor builds the total up from a single cask. What number ends the audit, in kJ?

A laboratory launcher is set from the curve y = 4x^3 - 4x^2. The technician first finds how fast the slope of that curve is itself changing at x = 1, then subtracts 23, then adds 9, and finally multiplies the result by 6. The value that comes out is the speed, in metres per second, of the trolley as it leaves the launcher. The trolley's mass plate reads 32000 g. What energy, in J, does the moving trolley carry?

A cheese dairy record ends with one number in joules. Two lots of 310 and 251 identical rounds are packed into equal full crates, using the largest crate size that divides both counts exactly. A trolley of mass 47 kg is then pushed at a speed, in metres per second, numerically equal to that crate size. The energy the moving trolley carries is the raw reading, to which 5 J stored in the door spring is added. Eleven trolleys work a store and the dairy has 4 stores, so the dairy figure is 11 times the corrected value and then 4 times that, after which a final 2 J is added for the weigh gate. A 500 L brine tank stands in the store and is not involved. What number ends the record, in J?

A florist's tally ends with one number in joules. Two consignments of 55 and 266 identical stems are made up into equal full bunches, using the largest bunch size that divides both counts exactly. Adding 1 to that bunch size gives the speed, in metres per second, of a delivery trolley of mass 20 kg. The energy the moving trolley carries is the base value. Eleven trolleys work the shop, so the shop energy is 11 times that base value, and 24 J is then subtracted for the door closer. What number ends the tally, in J?

A cable-car depot record ends with one number in kilojoules. A test carrier of mass 6 kg moves at a speed, in metres per second, equal to the exact area under the curve y = 4x^2 + 2x between x = 1 and x = 2. The energy the moving carrier carries is the base value, which the record writes in kilojoules. Three corrections are then applied in turn, all in those same kilojoule units: 26 is added for the drive house, 9 is subtracted for the meter tare, and 22 is added for the standby set. What number ends the record, in kJ?

A dry dock report ends with one number in newtons. A gate section of mass 193 kg is driven along its track. The control curve is y = 2x^3 + 5x^2, and the acceleration applied to the section, in metres per second squared, is how fast the slope of that curve is itself changing at x = 2. The ram must supply the force that gives that section that acceleration; from it 27 N of seal drag is subtracted, and 18 N of hinge preload is then added. Eight sections make a gate, and the dock has 5 gates. A 2000 L sump serves the dock and is not involved. What number ends the report, in N?

A saw mill record ends with one number in kilonewtons. Two orders of 22 and 267 identical planks are stacked into equal full piles, using the largest pile size that divides both counts exactly. A carriage of mass 177 kg is then accelerated at a rate, in metres per second squared, numerically equal to that pile size. The feed must supply the force that gives that carriage that acceleration. Three carriages run on the mill, so the mill force is 3 times one carriage's figure, from which 26 N is subtracted for the guide drag. The record writes the remainder in kilonewtons, then subtracts 19 in those same kilonewton units as the frame tare. What number ends the record, in kN?

A ropeway test accelerates a cabin of mass 155 kg at a rate, in metres per second squared, equal to the larger root of x^2 - 7x + 6 = 0. The haul cable must supply the force that gives that cabin that acceleration, and the log writes that force in kilonewtons. To the record 3 is added for the drive tension, and 28 is then subtracted for the counterweight, both in those same kilonewton units. The station's fuel store holds 250 L, which is no part of the test. What does the log finally show, in kN?

A dockside sheet ends with one number in kilonewtons. A crate whose mass plate reads 156000 g is accelerated at a rate, in metres per second squared, equal to the smaller root of x^2 - 8x + 15 = 0. The hoist must supply the force that gives that crate that acceleration, and 8 N of sling preload is added to it. The sheet writes that loaded force in kilonewtons, then subtracts 21 and adds 20, both in those same kilonewton units, as the two standing corrections. A 400 L fuel drum sits on the quay and is not involved. What number ends the sheet, in kN?

A seed store groups two lots of 238 and 21 identical sacks into equal full pallets, using the largest pallet size that divides both counts exactly. A trolley whose mass plate reads 19000 g is then accelerated at a rate, in metres per second squared, numerically equal to that pallet size. The pusher must supply the force that gives the trolley that acceleration, and the log records that force in kilonewtons. Four trolleys work an aisle, so the aisle figure is 4 times the record, and 16 is added in those same kilonewton units for the door gear. The store has 11 aisles. A 75 L dressing tank stands by the door and is not involved. What is the store total, in kN?

A laboratory report ends with one number in newtons. A slider of mass 8 kg runs on an air rail. The exact area under the curve y = 1x^2 + 1x between x = 1 and x = 3 is taken first, and adding 24 to that area gives the slider's acceleration in metres per second squared. The rail drive must supply the force that gives the slider that acceleration. Four sliders run per bench, and the laboratory has 11 benches. A 6 L compressed-air bottle feeds the rail and is not part of the calculation. What number ends the report, in N?

A funicular test uses a car whose mass plate reads 58000 g. The control curve is y = 4x^3 + 5x^2, and how fast the slope of that curve is itself changing at x = 2 is found first; subtracting 23 from that value gives the car's speed in metres per second. The energy the moving car carries is the raw reading, from which 3 J is subtracted for the brake shoe. The display writes the remainder in kilojoules, then adds 7 in those same kilojoule units as the machine allowance. What does the display show, in kJ?

A hoist bench accelerates a weight whose mass plate reads 15000 g at a rate, in metres per second squared, equal to the smaller root of x^2 - 15x + 56 = 0. The cable must supply the force that gives that weight that acceleration. Seven such weights hang from the same beam, so the beam force is 7 times one weight's figure, and the sheet writes that in kilonewtons. To the record 6 is then added, in those same kilonewton units, as the beam tare. The bench's oil can holds 2 L, which plays no part. What number does the sheet show, in kN?

A ski club's tally ends with one number in kilojoules. A sled of mass 6 kg runs at a speed, in metres per second, found by writing out 2k - 1 for k running from 1 to 6 and adding the six values together. The energy the moving sled carries is the base value, which the tally writes in kilojoules. Two sleds run per lane and 5 lanes are in use, so the hill figure is 2 times the record and then 5 times that. From that total 15 is subtracted, in those same kilojoule units, as the lift allowance. The club hut has a 25 L urn that plays no part. What number ends the tally, in kJ?

A bakery rack whose mass plate reads 33000 g is pushed along the floor. Its acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the smaller root of x^2 - 5x + 4 = 0. The pusher must supply the force that gives that rack that acceleration. Six racks are moved together, so the gang force is 6 times one rack's figure, and the log writes that in kilonewtons. To the record 10 is added for the door gear and then 16 for the ramp, both in those same kilonewton units. The proofing cabinet holds 120 L of air, which is not involved. What does the log finally show, in kN?
